title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A crystal‑clear Betty board capture of a high‑octane 2/18/71 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star→Wharf Rat→Dark Star jam and blistering Bertha.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller “Betty” soundboard release delivers superb fidelity – every instrument sits in the mix with remarkable clarity. The performance is a burst of 1971 energy, driven by an incendiary Dark Star/Wharf Rat sandwich, a fierce Bertha and a fast‑paced set that feels both historic and exhilarating. While a few tunes (e.g., Mama Tried, Casey Jones) show minor slips, the overall vibe remains overwhelmingly positive.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise both the recording (crisp, excellent mix) and the show (high energy, standout jams). A few lower‑rated comments note minor performance flaws, pulling the average down slightly but not enough to offset the strong consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Betty board (SBD) source; reviewers describe it as crisp, clear, with great dynamics and a well‑balanced mix. Minor quirks mentioned by a handful of listeners but overall considered one of the best‑sounding 1971 tapes.

standout_songs: Dark Star > Wharf Rat > Dark Star (Beautiful Jam)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set launches with high‑octane Bertha and a string of classic ‘71 cuts; second set builds around the epic Dark Star/Wharf Rat sandwich and finishes strong with Uncle John's Band. The pacing is fast, compact, and keeps momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as perfect, fast‑paced, gritty and full of bite; his use of wah/uni‑vibe pedals noted during the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s Hammond organ presence is highlighted (though some debate Ned Lagin’s clavichord/electric piano contributions).
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s last show for several years; drum sound praised as classic ‘71 power.
